traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Cycas revoluta (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.28 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 3 records in 1 source); trunks 0.28, branches 0.37. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a stout, shaggy trunk up to 2 to 3 m, very slow, under a crown of stiff, glossy, dark green feather fronds about 1 to 1.5 m long, with narrow, sharp leaflets curled under at the edges; a cone 30 to 60 cm long at the centre of a mature plant; suckers at the foot. Grown in gardens; native to southern Japan. Refitted from Whitelock (2002, p. 80, 138-139) and Kaplan (2022, p. 789-791): a flush of about sixteen leaves a year (at least one flush a year in gardens, two or more in the tropics), each rising straight with its leaflets coiled, not unrolling as a fern's frond does; a petiole of 5 to 7 cm on a leaf of 0.6 to 1.5 m, armed with spines; about seventy pairs of leaflets (60 to 150 in floras) set forward at about 45 degrees on a keeled rachis, so the two rows stand in a V; leaf stubs kept on the trunk for its life. Not otherwise fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 1.6 m at 30 years and 2.6 m at 60. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: dark glossy green fronds, a tan cone, brown leaf bases.
